You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement. People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples. Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments. Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.

messages.content:
You check an illustration plan before it is drawn. You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as a speaker, writer, prophet or listener put into a scene their words only describe or made a figure of their own words, the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.
For each problem, copy a short exact phrase from a scene field or a selected id into planQuote (from an owner constraint for look_conflict) and give a one-sentence reason.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Simon Peter; The Twelve Disciples (collective)

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Simon Peter: a sturdy man in his thirties, broad-shouldered from hauling nets, weathered brown skin from sun on the Sea of Galilee, short dark curly hair and a full beard flecked with grey. Plain undyed tunic of natural linen under a rough brown wool cloak. Signature props: a coiled fishing net over one shoulder and a wooden fishing staff.
- The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.
- Sea of Galilee: a large freshwater lake set in hilly terrain of basalt and limestone, its shores sloping to pebbled and sandy beaches. Low stone-built fishing villages and wooden fishing boats line the water, with nets drying on the shore. Reeds, oleanders and palms grow along the banks, and fig and olive trees climb the hills above.
- Only Simon Peter, The Twelve Disciples (collective), Sea of Galilee have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Disciples in damp fishermen's tunics stepping from the small wooden boat onto the sand, eyes fixed on the fire.
Action: They disembark and halt, seeing the glowing charcoal fire with fish and bread laid on it.
Setting: Sandy shore of the Sea of Galilee beside a small wooden fishing boat, with stone village roofs visible inland.
Secondary elements: A glowing charcoal fire on the beach, loaves and fish resting on it, a net heaped in the bottom of the boat, the lake glinting behind.
Mood: Quiet wonder and stunned recognition, tender and hushed.
Time of day: Early dawn with light morning mist lifting off the water, sky brightening toward sunrise.
Composition: Wide view from the water's edge looking up the beach, boat in the foreground, fire centred on the sand, figures spread across the middle distance.

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

- Image 1: Sea of Galilee's reference sheet (two views of the same place or thing). Match its identity exactly for Sea of Galilee only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.

Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

- Before: But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away), dragging the net full of fish.

You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church. People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule. Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing. Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.

STORY SECTION: Peter denies Jesus
ON STAGE: Simon Peter, Crowd in Luke, the court of the high priest (Caiaphas)
TEXT OF THE SECTION'S FIRST MOMENT (the look covers the whole section):
The Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the Lord’s word, how he said to him, “Before the rooster crows you will deny me three times.”

content.text:
PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Exodus 17:12: "But Moses’ hands were heavy; so they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His hands were steady until sunset."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement
People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples.
Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments.
Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.
Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Moses; Aaron, brother of Moses; Hur; The Israelite people (the children of Israel); Amalekites; Joshua son of Nun

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.
- Hur: man in his fifties to sixties, sturdy and weathered from desert travel; medium build with strong, steady arms; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked dark hair and a trimmed grey beard; calm, dignified face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain woven undertunic of undyed cream linen under a rust-brown wool cloak. No props.
- The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.
- Amalekites: a typical warrior of a desert people, adult, aged roughly twenty-five to forty; lean, weathered build; sun-darkened olive-brown skin; dark hair tied back, short beard kept close; strong, wind-creased face with a steady gaze. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic belted with leather, over it a sand-coloured woven cloak in ochre and brown. Carries a curved sword at the belt and a leather shield as their own props.
- Rephidim: a wide, dry valley of pale sand and broken limestone in the Sinai wilderness, bordered by low, rust-coloured cliffs. A single great rock face of dark grey granite rises at the valley's head, its surface cracked and streaked with mineral stains. Sparse thorn scrub and tufts of dry grass grow in the gullies, with a few stunted acacia trees near the rock. Distant peaks of Sinai show as blue-grey shapes on the horizon.
- Joshua son of Nun: a man of mature strength in his prime, aged about forty to fifty when leading, with a sturdy, broad-shouldered build and weathered brown skin marked by desert sun. Short dark hair, close-cropped beard, steady deep-set eyes and a firm, grave face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic and a dark brown woven wool cloak. Carries a bronze-bladed sword at his belt and a long wooden spear.
- Only Moses, Aaron, brother of Moses, Hur, The Israelite people (the children of Israel), Amalekites, Rephidim, Joshua son of Nun have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Moses seated on a flat stone, arms raised and supported by Aaron and Hur
Action: Aaron and Hur steady Moses' tired arms while the Israelite warriors press the battle below
Setting: A dry rocky valley at Rephidim with tents at the edge and dusty battle lines
Secondary elements: Joshua leading Israelite warriors in the mid-ground, Amalekite fighters in tribal dress, dust clouds rising
Mood: Strained, determined, quietly hopeful and reverent
Time of day: Late afternoon sun in a hot, dry, clear sky with dust in the air, warm light toward sunset
Composition: Wide view from the valley floor looking up at Moses on his stone, with Aaron and Hur flanking him and the battle spread across the middle ground

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
- Image 2: Aaron, brother of Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Aaron, brother of Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
- Image 3: Joshua son of Nun's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Joshua son of Nun only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed. When he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.
- After: Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Kinds:

You plan one illustration of one moment of a work's text. You get the moment with its neighbours in the same story section, the work brief, the era, the section cast and a SECTION LOOK GUIDE. Return only JSON.
- Draw one scene at one instant: no collage and no sequence of steps. If the moment recounts several actions, pick one representative instant. If it has no event (a list, genealogy, law, saying or greeting), illustrate its content or setting through people, places and things, never as a written document.
- Show what the moment is about. When the moment is mostly someone's words (a prophecy, oracle, poem, proverb, prayer, letter, argument or teaching, or a story, parable, vision or memory being told), draw what the words describe and leave the speaker, writer and listeners out, unless the text shows them inside that scene (a visionary within the vision). Never put a speaker, writer or listener into a scene their words only describe, and never make them a figure of their own words, such as the king ready for battle or the man standing in the gap.
- In `selectedCast`, list every section cast entry that will be visible: people, groups, places, objects, and any presence without form shown through its effects. Give a few words of the text for each. Leave out cast who are elsewhere or only mentioned. Anyone without a cast entry may appear as an unnamed role or crowd when the moment needs them.
- Describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Leave fixed appearance to canon, name no art style, and ask for no visible writing: scrolls, tablets, letters and books stay rolled or closed, and signs and boards are blank. Describe only what can be seen; leave out unseen or invisible beings, because anything named gets drawn. Keep every depiction rule.
- The scene fields carry this moment's place, time, light and situational clothing. The SECTION LOOK GUIDE is a suggestion for them: keep what fits this moment and change what does not. OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS, when given instead, are binding: keep the setting and time of day consistent with them.
- Each field is one or two short phrases.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Numbers 20:11: "Moses lifted up his hand, and struck the rock with his rod twice, and water came out abundantly. The congregation and their livestock drank."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement
People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples.
Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments.
Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.
Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Moses; Aaron, brother of Moses; The Israelite people (the children of Israel)

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.
- The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.
- Kadesh: a desert oasis in the wilderness of Zin at the edge of Edom's border, a wide basin of pale sand and gravel ringed by low rocky ridges. A spring wells from the rock beside a cluster of goat-hair tents and a few mud-brick walls of a settlement. Tamarisk, acacia and scattered palms grow near the water; beyond, the bare hills of the wilderness rise.
- Only Moses, Aaron, brother of Moses, The Israelite people (the children of Israel), Kadesh (Kadesh Barnea) have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Moses standing tall before the rock, rod raised high in his right hand mid-strike
Action: Water bursts from the rock in a strong abundant stream as the people gather to drink
Setting: An oasis at Kadesh with a spring welling from the rock beside goat-hair tents, tamarisk, acacia and palms
Secondary elements: Aaron at Moses's side in priestly linen; Israelites with livestock crowding forward, filling jars and cupping hands; a dusty crowd in woven wool tunics and cloaks
Mood: Reverent relief and awe as thirst gives way to abundance
Time of day: Midday, sun high and hot, clear dry air with a little dust
Composition: Wide view from the crowd's side, rock and Moses central, water arcing across the foreground, people and animals spread across the frame

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
- Image 2: Kadesh (Kadesh Barnea)'s reference sheet (two views of the same place or thing). Match its identity exactly for Kadesh (Kadesh Barnea) only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
- Image 3: Aaron, brother of Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Aaron, brother of Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly together before the rock, and he said to them, “Hear now, you rebels! Shall we bring water out of this rock for you?”
- After: Yahweh said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you didn’t believe in me, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land which I have given them.”

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Luke 22:61: "The Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the Lord’s word, how he said to him, “Before the rooster crows you will deny me three times.”"

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Simon Peter; Crowd in Luke

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Simon Peter: a sturdy man in his thirties, broad-shouldered from hauling nets, weathered brown skin from sun on the Sea of Galilee, short dark curly hair and a full beard flecked with grey. Plain undyed tunic of natural linen under a rough brown wool cloak. Signature props: a coiled fishing net over one shoulder and a wooden fishing staff.
- Crowd in Luke: a typical member is an ordinary adult of Judean or Galilean village life, from young adult to middle age, lean and sun-worn, with olive or brown skin, dark hair kept short or tied back, and a short beard or clean-shaven face; plain undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, undyed cream and earth brown, with a woollen cloak and a head covering; carries no props of their own.
- The court of the high priest: an open paved courtyard of pale limestone flagstones inside a high-walled stone house in Jerusalem. A wide arched gateway with a timber door faces the street. A charcoal fire burns on a stone hearth at the centre of the court, and a stone porch with columns stands along one side. Olive and fig trees grow in clay pots by the walls; the upper walls are plastered and lit by torch sconces.
- Only Simon Peter, Crowd in Luke, the court of the high priest (Caiaphas) have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Simon Peter standing near the fire, face turned toward Jesus, his expression stricken with sudden recognition.
Action: Jesus turns and looks steadily at Peter across the courtyard as Peter's denial falls silent.
Setting: Stone courtyard of the high priest's house, with a central fire of coals and a torch-lit passage leading to the gate.
Secondary elements: Soldiers and temple guards in the background by the fire, a bound Jesus visible at the passage edge, a faint rooster silhouetted on a low wall.
Mood: Sorrowful, tense and intimate, with grief and dawning remorse.
Time of day: Deep night before dawn, cool damp air, warm firelight against cold darkness with a first grey glow beyond the walls.
Composition: Peter in the foreground near the fire, Jesus in the middle distance across the courtyard, eyes meeting along a diagonal line of sight.

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Simon Peter's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Simon Peter only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
- Image 2: the court of the high priest (Caiaphas)'s reference sheet (two views of the same place or thing). Match its identity exactly for the court of the high priest (Caiaphas) only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: But Peter said, “Man, I don’t know what you are talking about!” Immediately, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
- After: He went out, and wept bitterly.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Samuel; David son of Jesse (king of Israel); Jesse; Eliab; Abinadab son of Jesse; Shammah

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Samuel: a man in his middle years, lean and upright, with weathered brown skin, a close-trimmed dark beard flecked with grey, short hair and calm, steady eyes. His signature outfit is a long undyed linen tunic belted at the waist under a deep blue wool cloak. He carries a horn of oil at his belt and, on journeys, a plain wooden staff.
- David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.
- Jesse: an elderly man of Bethlehem in Judah, past sixty, lean and upright from years of labour; olive-brown skin weathered by sun; short grey beard close to the jaw; grey hair under a plain head-cloth; deep lines around the eyes and a steady, serious face. Signature outfit: an undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a dark brown woollen cloak with a thick fringe at the hem. Carries a shepherd's staff of dark wood; no other props alone.
- Eliab: man in his twenties, tall and broad-shouldered from years of shepherding and soldiering; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and a trimmed beard; strong brow, straight nose and a set, stern mouth. Signature outfit: a sleeveless tunic of undyed linen under a rust-red cloak, with bronze scale armor on the shoulders. Carries a round bronze shield and a short sword.
- Abinadab son of Jesse: man in his twenties; sturdy, broad-shouldered build; olive-brown skin; dark curly hair and short beard; steady, serious face with a strong nose. Signature outfit: undyed linen tunic with a plain blue-grey wool cloak. Carries no props alone.
- Shammah: a young man of about twenty, lean and sinewy from shepherding and soldiering; medium height; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard; calm, steady features with a serious, dignified bearing. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a deep ochre woollen cloak. Signature prop: a leather sling.
- Bethlehem Judah: a walled hill town on a limestone ridge in the hill country of Judah, flat-roofed stone and mud-brick houses climbing terraced slopes, a city gate of heavy timber and stone where elders sit, olive groves and vineyards on the terraces, barley fields in the valley below, and a well outside the walls.
- Only Samuel, David son of Jesse (king of Israel), Jesse, Eliab, Abinadab son of Jesse, Shammah, Bethlehem Judah have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Samuel in priestly linen tilting a horn of oil over the bowed head of young David
Action: The oil is poured onto David's head as the moment of anointing unfolds.
Setting: Open courtyard of a Bethlehem house beside a sheepfold, stone walls and village dwellings
Secondary elements: Jesse and his older sons standing close together to one side, a crook and sheep at the edge of the fold
Mood: Solemn, hushed and expectant with quiet dignity
Time of day: Late afternoon, clear dry air, warm low golden sunlight with long soft shadows
Composition: Samuel and David centered in the foreground, brothers arranged in a loose half-circle behind, village walls framing the scene

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Samuel's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Samuel only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
- Image 2: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)'s reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for David son of Jesse (king of Israel) only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, 1 Samuel 17:40: "He took his staff in his hand, and chose for himself five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag which he had. His sling was in his hand; and he came near to the Philistine."

Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.

Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.

Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: David son of Jesse (king of Israel); Goliath

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.
- Goliath: man of enormous height, over nine feet tall, broad-shouldered and heavily muscled, around forty years old. Olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a full dark beard, strong heavy brow, grave and hard features. Wears bronze scale armour over a linen tunic, bronze greaves, and a bronze helmet, colours of bronze, dark leather and undyed linen. Carries a great spear with a heavy iron head and a sword at his side.
- Valley of Elah: a broad, shallow valley of the Judean lowlands between rounded hills of terraced limestone, with a dry watercourse winding through its floor. Scattered terebinth and oak trees and low scrub grow along the slopes, and sun-baked earth shows pale between rocks. Rough stone walls and simple dwellings of field stone mark the hill ridges.
- Only David son of Jesse (king of Israel), Goliath, Valley of Elah have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: David, young and slight, selecting stones with his staff in one hand and sling in the other
Action: Picking smooth stones from the brook into his pouch, then turning toward the approaching Philistine champion
Setting: Dry stony brook bed in the Valley of Elah between hillsides, scattered terebinth trees
Secondary elements: Shepherd's leather bag, staff leaning nearby, faint distant shape of Goliath in bronze armor approaching across the wadi
Mood: Quiet resolve, tense calm before danger
Time of day: Midday shifting toward late afternoon, clear hot sky, harsh golden sunlight with short shadows
Composition: Low viewpoint from the brook bed, David in the foreground bending over the stones, Goliath small in the middle distance

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)'s reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for David son of Jesse (king of Israel) only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: David strapped his sword on his clothing and he tried to move, for he had not tested it. David said to Saul, “I can’t go with these, for I have not tested them.” Then David took them off.
- After: The Philistine walked and came near to David; and the man who bore the shield went before him.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Daniel 5:17: "Then Daniel answered before the king, “Let your gifts be to yourself, and give your rewards to another. Nevertheless, I will read the writing to the king, and make known to him the interpretation."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Daniel (prophet of Babylon); Belshazzar

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Daniel: a lean, dignified Judean man, grave and greying; olive-brown skin; close-cropped greying hair and a short trimmed grey beard; deep-set, steady eyes and a calm, thoughtful face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a plain indigo wool cloak with a blue fringed hem. Props: a small leather scroll case slung at the hip.
- Belshazzar: a man in his thirties or early forties, of lean, upright build; olive-bronze skin; short dark hair and a neatly curled beard in the Mesopotamian royal manner; a strong brow and deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long fringed royal robe of deep crimson wool over a white linen tunic, with a tall, pleated, gold-banded crown. Carries a gold-hilted ceremonial dagger at the belt.
- Royal palace of Babylon: a vast walled complex on the flat alluvial plain of the Euphrates, built of sun-dried and fired brick glazed in deep blue with yellow lion and dragon reliefs. Tiered terraces rise toward a great gate with tall towers; hanging gardens of palms, date trees and climbing vines spill over the walls. Broad courts of pale stone lead to a banquet hall with high cedar-beamed ceilings and a river-facing colonnade.
- Only Daniel (prophet of Babylon), Belshazzar, Royal palace of Babylon have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Daniel in plain linen and cloak, standing upright and composed before the king, one hand raised in refusal.
Action: Daniel declines the royal gifts and rewards and prepares to read and interpret the writing.
Setting: Royal banquet hall of the palace of Babylon with tall pillars, glazed tiles and lamp-lit alcoves.
Secondary elements: Belshazzar seated on a raised couch in a fringed royal robe of deep crimson wool over white linen, gold-banded crown on his head; nobles in court robes at the edges; gilded vessels on a low table; a blank tablet-like wall panel with no visible writing.
Mood: Tense and solemn, with dignity and quiet resolve under the glitter of the feast.
Time of day: Night during a feast, still warm air, warm lamplight and torches with cool darkness beyond the doorways.
Composition: Medium shot from the side, Daniel in the foreground left facing the seated king at right, pillars framing the hall and the lamp-lit depth behind.

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Daniel (prophet of Babylon)'s reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Daniel (prophet of Babylon) only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
- Image 2: Royal palace of Babylon's reference sheet (two views of the same place or thing). Match its identity exactly for Royal palace of Babylon only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- After: “To you, king, the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father the kingdom, and greatness, and glory, and majesty.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as a speaker, writer, prophet or listener put into a scene their words only describe or made a figure of their own words, the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.
For each problem, copy a short exact phrase from a scene field or a selected id into planQuote (from an owner constraint for look_conflict) and give a one-sentence reason.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Luke 15:22: "“But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: The prodigal's father; the younger son

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- The prodigal's father: man in his late fifties to sixties, of middle height and sturdy, weathered build from years of farm labour; olive skin, lined with sun; close-cropped grey-streaked dark hair and a short greying beard; deep-set, kind eyes and a broad, steady face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a dark russet woollen cloak, with a fringed tzitzit at the hem. Signature props: none carried alone; a bronze signet ring on his hand.
- the younger son: Young man in his late teens or early twenties, slender and wiry, with a lean build. Olive skin browned by travel and weather. Dark hair cut short and unkempt, with a short, sparse beard. Face young and open, with weary eyes and a tired mouth. Signature outfit: a sun-faded undyed linen tunic with a dust-brown woollen cloak. Signature prop: a small leather purse at his belt.
- Galilee: Northern hill country falling to a freshwater lake, the sea of Galilee, its shore lined with fishing boats and nets drying on stone. Low limestone villages of flat-roofed houses, a white stone synagogue with a shallow portico, terraced olive groves, fig trees and scrubland. Roman roads and a distant Gentile town on the slopes.
- Only The prodigal's father, the younger son, Galilee have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: The elderly father, arms open, standing at the courtyard gate as the younger son kneels before him
Action: The father gives a command to servants, who move to fetch a robe, a ring and sandals
Setting: Stone farmstead courtyard in Galilee with a low stone wall and terraced hills beyond
Secondary elements: Two servants in simple tunics hurrying toward a doorway; the son's dusty travel-worn garments; a clay water jar nearby
Mood: Tender, relieved and dignified, with grief easing into welcome
Time of day: Late afternoon, clear and dry, with a light breeze
Composition: Wide framing from the courtyard side, father and kneeling son central, servants moving to one side, low sun casting long shadows

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
- After: Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let’s eat and celebrate;

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).
